quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle that could enter your path will do so.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together as a group while leaving enough space around each rider. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Riding in pairs does not allow enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: How should you choose your lane position?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.
Always ride in the right part of the lane.
Base your choice on many different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Base your choice on many different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you are most likely to be seen and where you can keep space around you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which makes your motorcycle respond more slowly. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if it starts to rain while riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that become slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Reduce your speed on wet surfaces.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when exiting a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for most group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: In the left part of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, cover the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets more experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction of your turn causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: On a wet road, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. When the road is wet, this oily strip is slippery. You can ride on the sides of the center portion and still stay in the lane safely.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop, if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if heavy traffic means another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and moving straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How powerful are motorcycle headlights compared to car headlights?
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When should you apply your brakes?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If conditions make stopping longer than normal, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where drivers might cut in front of you. Keep at least a three-second distance.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn.
questions.explanation: Hand signals show your intentions to turn or stop. If your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing up, it means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.
Press the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to stop a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking and let them sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Good ways to prevent drunk driving include: arranging another ride, keeping them busy with other activities, finding any reason to keep them from leaving, and getting friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes does not work because alcohol takes much longer to leave the body.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color makes you most visible?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be seen better. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. The rear wheel should touch the curb.
